residencyRequirements.description: At least one party must have been a bona fide resident of the State of Delaware for at least six months before the commencement of the proceeding.

waitingPeriod.description: Delaware has no mandatory waiting period after filing for divorce.

noFault.name: Irretrievable Breakdown
noFault.description: The marriage is irretrievably broken, as demonstrated by reconciliation being improbable or the parties having lived separate and apart for at least six months

groundsForDissolution.notes: Delaware is a purely no-fault state. The only ground for divorce is irretrievable breakdown of the marriage. This can be demonstrated by showing that reconciliation is improbable, or that the parties have voluntarily lived separate and apart for six or more months without reasonable expectation of reconciliation.

propertyDivision.description: Delaware courts divide marital property equitably. The court considers factors including the length of the marriage, any prior marriage of either party, the age, health, station, amount and sources of income, vocational skills, employability, estate, liabilities, and needs of each party, and whether the property award is in lieu of or in addition to alimony.
propertyDivision.separateProperty: Property acquired before the marriage, by inheritance, or by gift (excluding gifts between the spouses) is generally considered separate property and is not subject to division, although the court has discretion.

legalCitations.description: Grounds for divorce — irretrievable breakdown only (no-fault)
Division of marital property — equitable distribution

filingFees.notes: Delaware Family Court filing fee for divorce is $165 plus a $10 court security fee ($175 total). Fee waivers may be available for qualifying low-income individuals.

basic.name: Decree of Divorce
basic.description: Final court order dissolving the marriage

withChildren.name: Child Support Guidelines Worksheet (Melson Formula)
withChildren.description: Calculation per Delaware Melson Formula (Del. Code tit. 13, §514)

withChildren.name: Parenting Plan
withChildren.description: Plan for custody and residential arrangements

formattingRequirements.notes: Per Delaware Family Court Rules of Civil Procedure

inState.description: Respondent must file a response within 20 days of service

outOfState.description: Respondent served outside Delaware has 20 days to file a response

responseDeadlines.statute: Del. Family Court R. Civ. P. 12(a)

childSupportGuidelines.description: Delaware uses the Melson Formula, a unique variation of the income shares model. It provides each parent with a self-support allowance, calculates a primary support obligation based on each child's needs, and adds a standard of living adjustment. Delaware is one of only three states using the Melson Formula.
childSupportGuidelines.notes: The Melson Formula is more complex than standard income shares. It first ensures each parent can meet their own basic needs, then calculates child support obligations.

maintenanceGuidelines.description: Delaware courts may award alimony after considering factors including the financial needs of each party, the financial resources of each party, any marital misconduct, the duration of the marriage, the age and physical and emotional condition of the parties, and whether one party sacrificed career or educational opportunities for the other.
maintenanceGuidelines.eligibility: Available based on need and ability to pay. The dependent party must have insufficient property and be unable to support themselves through appropriate employment.

court.name: Family Court
court.description: Divorce cases are filed in the Family Court. (Del. Code tit. 10, §921)
